# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 5
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
12 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 2
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

**LOGOS (formal):** And Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon sent back this message to Hiram:

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** And-now, YHWH my-God has-given-rest to-me all-around; there-is-no adversary and-no evil occurrence.

**LOGOS (formal):** But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side. There is neither adversary nor misfortune.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But now the LORD my God has given me peace on every border. There is no enemy, no crisis.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-behold, I am-saying to-build a-house for-the-name-of YHWH my-God, as YHWH spoke to David my-father, saying, 'Your-son whom I-will-set in-your-place upon your-throne — he will-build the-house for-my-name.'

**LOGOS (formal):** Therefore I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD spoke to David my father, saying, 'Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place, shall build the house for my name.'

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** So I am planning to build a temple for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD told my father David: 'Your son, whom I will place on your throne after you — he is the one who will build the temple for my name.'

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-now, command that-they-cut for-me cedars from the-Lebanon. And-my-servants will-be with your-servants, and-the-wages-of your-servants I-will-give to-you according-to all that you-say. For you know that there-is-no man among-us who-knows to-cut timber like the-Sidonians."

**LOGOS (formal):** Now therefore command that cedars of Lebanon be cut for me. My servants will join your servants, and I will pay your servants' wages according to whatever you set. For you know that there is no one among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Please order that cedars of Lebanon be cut for me. My workers will work alongside yours, and I will pay your workers whatever wages you set. As you know, we have no one who can match the Sidonians at cutting timber."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was when Hiram heard ʾet-the-words-of Solomon, and-he-rejoiced greatly, and-said, "Blessed is YHWH today, who has-given to-David a-wise son over this great people."

**LOGOS (formal):** When Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly and said, "Blessed be the LORD this day, who has given David a wise son over this great people."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** When Hiram received Solomon's message, he was overjoyed. "Praise the LORD today," he said, "for giving David a wise son to rule this great nation!"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, "I-have-heard ʾet what you-sent to-me. I will-do all your-desire concerning timber-of cedar and-timber-of cypress.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, "I have heard the message you have sent to me. I will fulfill all your desire for cedar timber and cypress timber.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Hiram sent his reply to Solomon: "I received your message. I will supply everything you need in cedar and cypress timber.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** My-servants will-bring-them-down from the-Lebanon to the-sea, and-I will-make-them into-rafts on-the-sea to the-place that you-send to-me, and-I-will-break-them-up there. And-you will-carry them away. And-you will-do my-desire, to-give food for-my-household."

**LOGOS (formal):** My servants shall bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts to go by sea to the place you direct. I will have them broken up there, and you shall carry them away. And you shall meet my desire by providing food for my household."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** My men will haul the logs from Lebanon down to the coast, where I'll have them lashed into rafts and floated by sea to wherever you specify. I'll have them broken apart there for you to collect. In return, you will supply food for my palace."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 11
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon gave to-Hiram twenty thousand cors-of wheat as-food for-his-household, and-twenty cors-of beaten oil. Thus Solomon gave to-Hiram year by-year.

**LOGOS (formal):** while Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram year by year.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** and Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat and twenty cors of pure olive oil annually for his household.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 13
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Solomon raised a-labor-levy from-all Israel. And-the-levy was thirty thousand men.

**LOGOS (formal):** King Solomon drafted forced labor out of all Israel, and the draft numbered thirty thousand men.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** King Solomon conscripted laborers from all over Israel — thirty thousand men.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** besides Solomon's chief officers who were over the-work — three thousand three hundred who-ruled over the-people who-did the-work.

**LOGOS (formal):** besides Solomon's three thousand three hundred chief officers who were over the work, who had charge of the people doing the work.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** plus thirty-three hundred foremen who supervised the workers.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king commanded, and-they-quarried great stones, costly stones, to-lay-the-foundation-of the-house with-hewn stones.

**LOGOS (formal):** At the king's command, they quarried great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with dressed stones.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** On the king's orders, they quarried large blocks of high-quality stone to lay a dressed-stone foundation for the temple.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-the-builders-of Solomon and-the-builders-of Hiram and-the-Gebalites cut-them, and-they-prepared the-timber and-the-stones to-build the-house.

**LOGOS (formal):** So Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders and the men of Gebal cut and prepared the timber and the stone to build the house.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and craftsmen from Gebal shaped and prepared the timber and stone for the construction.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
